title: Search multiple indices with combined results in one hits area
body:
Through Algolia's API I can see that [it is possible to query multiple indices](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-client/javascript/search/#search-multiple-indices).
But is it possible to have two sets of results ranked against each other?

The main use case is, you have two indexes of data with different properties, but you want to give the user the ability to see results from both **and ranked against each other** (this is key). 

You could add multiple indexes when configuring instant search:
```
instantsearch({
  appId: config.appId,
  apiKey: config.apiKey,
  indexNames: ['index1','index2'] 
});
```
Now each query would apply a search to both, and return a combined result that ranks them against each other.

I'm sure there are complications in being able to rank two different structures against each other, but often you have very different data sets and want to embed along with them some other kind of data.

One example would be, you have an index of web pages, and you have an index of company locations.
You want a user to be able to search the web pages for specific content, but if their search matches company locations, you want to highlight those in order of relevance to other web page results to the user.

Could something like this be done by creating a custom instantsearch widget where you manually combined two sets of results in some fashion?

comments.body:
I found this discussion: ["Compare ranking of Algolia query across multiple indices"](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32615483/compare-ranking-of-algolia-query-across-multiple-indices)
Perhaps what I am looking for is better done by combining data into 1 index, and then querying that index.
Hi @Giovanni-Mattucci thanks for your issue. I'm sorry but you can't have records from different indices and aggregate them in a single list with Algolia.
Hi @Giovanni-Mattucci  , what did you end up doing? Our use case is that we have two indexes from the same data but we do not want to match the query on the same fields. Does that ring a bell?

You have some options:

- mix the indices, and make sure they have the same shape
- use two different indices, with the index component in separate lists and have your UI distinguish between the two
- use multi-index to search through both indices, then re-sort them frontend based on your own algorithm

Unfortunately there's no builtin way to consolidate ranking across different criteria, as there's no way to sort those.

Thank you @Haroenv , we are indeed trying to find a solution to mix the indices a single search request, because frontend solutions will not work for us (mostly because we need to paginate over 1000 results).

Infortunately we need to run a query over different fields, so this looks like a dead end.
Does it _need_ to be different fields? can you not alias both to a single set of consistent fields?

I am not sure I follow you. We need to search "foo" in fields A,B,C and "bar" in fields B,C,D. We must _not_ match "foo" in field D and "bar" in field A.

How I understand things is that if you want to be able to have ranked results and correct pagination server side:
*  you must use only one request
* to match those fields you need to use the `query` (those are not facets)
* a single query means a single set of fields to match from.

Am I missing something here?

(Thank you for taking the time!)

The two indexes have the same data actually, they just happen to have different `searchable_attributes`. Not sure why it has been made this way because we can override that parameter on resquest.

And you will find records like this:

```json
{
  "favorite_foods": ["apples","oranges","bread"],
  "description": "I love to foo and also bar"
}
{
  "favorite_foods": ["aples","ORANGES!!"],
  "description": "Just foo for me"
}
```

And a user query = `?keywords=foo bar&foods=apples oranges`. So we were doing two requests, one to match the `keywords` on all fields, and the `foods` on `favorite_foods` only. (Made up example, in reality there are more fields involved, but at least one of the two queries MUST NOT search in all the searchable fields of the other query. Not sure about the other query).

In the UI, do you have two separate search boxes for this then? or are you relying only on the URL and there's no ui to set these queries?

For me favorite_foods seems more like a use case for facets than for search. I wonder if you can normalise the values first so they don't have misspellings, before indexing. Then you can use `filters` or `facetFilters` for the `favorite_foods` attribute, and `query` for the full text search.

Are the favorite foods coming from user input? 

Alternatively you could also add a rule on the "matches facet" for favorite foods and then apply that facet, remove the word from the query, if there's only one input: https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/managing-results/rules/detecting-intent/

In search there's only one query, because there's only one actual search happening. This is because if you don't share a query, you can't compare the sets of results, and therefore also wouldn't be able to show the most relevant results.

Hope this helps, but it may be interesting to contact your solutions engineer for more a more in-depth conversation.

Yeah sorry the example is not great but favorite food is indeed user submitted text. 

We cannot use facets in there. We have two search boxes in the UI yes, that lead to two query string properties, but only one resultset in the UI, we cannot split the results in two panels for instance.

We could normalize those foods. We discussed it and found another problem but I can't remember it. It's still a possible solution though, but it is not what we want.

We are also discussing using weighted results instead, searching "foo" in favorite foods but with much less score impact.

And yes, I guess the Algolia team could help us on that!
